Eddy current and tube inspection in Baton Rouge: exchanger bundles at turnaround

Most eddy current work in Baton Rouge is heat-exchanger tube inspection during refinery and chemical plant turnarounds, plus some surface crack checks on coated or non-magnetic parts. The tube material sets the technique: conventional ECT for non-ferrous tubes, remote field or near-field testing for carbon steel, and IRIS when remaining wall must be measured. Atlantis sends crews from Houston and reports under ASNT NDT Level III review.

Matching the technique to the bundle.

  • Bobbin ECT: fast on admiralty brass, copper-nickel, stainless and titanium tubes; finds pitting, wear at baffles and general thinning.
  • Remote field testing: for carbon steel and other ferromagnetic tubes; good on general wall loss, less sensitive to small isolated pits.
  • Near-field testing: for finned carbon steel tubes such as air coolers, aimed at internal pitting and erosion near the tube ends.
  • IRIS: an ultrasonic rotating head that measures remaining wall in any tube material; slower, and it needs clean tubes flooded with water, so it is usually used to prove up the worst tubes the faster screen found.

A sound tube inspection plan screens the whole bundle with the fast method, proves up a sample with IRIS, and agrees the plugging or retubing criteria with the owner before testing starts, so decisions do not wait for a meeting in the middle of the night shift.

Turnaround logistics. Bundles pulled during a turnaround go to the wash pad for hydroblasting, and tube inspection sits on the critical path between cleaning and reassembly. Probes will not pass scale or hardened deposits, so cleaning quality decides how much of the bundle can be tested. Ask for the tube sheet map, the percentage of tubes tested, the reason any tube was not tested, and the raw data files, not only a summary of plugged tubes.

Rules that shape the work. Louisiana falls under federal OSHA, not a State Plan, so the process safety management standard applies to covered units; heat exchangers are pressure vessels under its mechanical integrity element, and inspection frequency must follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practice and the plant's own experience. Humid air and warm cooling water speed up fouling and under-deposit corrosion, which is why repeat campaigns on the same bundles are worth comparing tube by tube.

Read about the method's strengths and blind spots on eddy current testing, and about measuring wall loss in steel bundles on IRIS tube inspection. Outage scopes that combine tube work with UT, PT and visual inspection are under turnaround and shutdown inspection. For technicians, ET training covers the method for SNT-TC-1A certification, the Practical NDT eddy current simulator gives signal practice, and Baton Rouge NDT training lists local options. To scope a campaign, send the bundle list, tube materials, sizes and turnaround dates through the Baton Rouge tube inspection request.
